title: Cutover Dry-Run Scenarios & Rollout Matrix (Prototype)
content:
Purpose:
This doc is a lightweight prototype for a scheduled cutover dry-run that validates the orchestration, monitoring, and rollback decision paths for a medium-risk deployment (model rollout + runtime change). Intended audience: release engineer on-call, SRE shift lead, product owner, and small ops observers.

Scope:
- Exercise fast-path canary (1% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100%) across two regions (us-east1, eu-west1)
- Validate prefix cache warmup, KV cache persistence across hot-restarts, and autoscaling triggers
- Test graceful fallback to prior model variant and lower-cost instance types

How to use this doc:
- Run the dry-run in the staging-cluster mapped to the same service account as prod (but with traffic cut).
- Record timings and anomalies in the attached runbook notes.
- After dry-run, fill the red-team checklist and schedule a 30-minute retrospective.

Scenario matrix (quick reference) - narrative form:
- Scenario A: Happy-path canary. Start at 1% traffic in us-east1 only for 30m. Expected: steady lat P50<P60ms, error rate <0.05%. No manual intervention.
- Scenario B: Cache regression. Introduce a synthetic request pattern that forces cold KV misses. Expected: temporary token cost spike, P95 latency bump to ~200ms, autoscaler should not thrash. Trigger: if P95 > 400ms for 10m -> rollback.
- Scenario C: Model quality regression. Deploy model variant with a deliberate edge-case prompt set; automated evals flag >5% quality regression vs baseline. Trigger immediate stop of rollout and demote traffic.
- Scenario D: Infra contention. Simulate node pressure (CPU/GPU) by background worker on a 10% subset. Expected: autoscale adds nodes per policy; if scale-up fails -> route to fallback region.

Timed dry-run calendar (single-day template) - local times are UTC:
- D-1 (prep)
  - 09:00: Confirm cutover roster and Slack bridge created (owner: Marcus Lee)
  - 10:00: Verify runbook artifacts and traffic mirror targets (owner: Asha Patel)
  - 14:00: Smoke tests on staging (quick list below) and alerting thresholds sanity (owner: SRE shift)
- Day 0 (dry-run)
  - 08:30: Final preflight call (15m): confirm abort conditions, who can approve roll-forward (owner: Release lead)
  - 09:00: Start canary @1% us-east1 (automated, observation window: 30m) (owner: automation)
  - 09:30: Decision checkpoint 1 (manual/auto): escalate if any fail criteria (owner: Release lead)
  - 10:00: Ramp to 10% in us-east1 & 1% eu-west1 (30m)
  - 11:00: Ramp to 50% (region-aware), run synthetic KV warmup for 15m
  - 12:00: Lunch hold (30m) - continue monitoring
  - 13:00: Ramp to 100% in primary region, 20% in secondary (observation 45m)
  - 14:00: Run chaos-lite test: introduce 5s storage latency on cache tier for 10m (owner: SRE)
  - 15:00: Evaluate metrics and roll to full if green; else trigger rollback drill
  - 16:00: Post-rollout verification tests and finalize release notes draft
  - 17:00: Short retro and capture action items

Preflight checklist (short):
- [ ] All PRs merged and green (CI: main branch status green)
- [ ] Canary config committed to infra repo with annotated owner and TTL
- [ ] Alerting runbooks linked in PagerDuty rotations
- [ ] Observability dashboards pinned and team bookmarks created
- [ ] Backfill tokens and cost cap alarms set (owner: finance buddy)

Smoke test list (run after 09:00 deploy):
- Basic text-generation end-to-end latency test (1k requests, median)
- Chat session KV persistence test (open, close, resume)
- Embeddings sanity check for high-dim vectors (compare distances)
- API contract tests (missing fields, error codes)

Gating criteria (abort conditions):
- Any increase in 5xx error rate >0.2% absolute over baseline for 10m
- P95 latency > 3x baseline for 5m
- Automated quality eval fails per preset prompt set (delta >5%)
- Autoscaler fail-to-add nodes for >10m in face of increased CPU/GPU demand

Rollback decision tree (textual):
- If gating criteria met at any checkpoint:
  1) Pause rollout and mark incident channel (owner: Release lead)
  2) Attempt targeted mitigation (clear cache, scale up fast path) for 5–10m
  3) If mitigation unsuccessful, initiate rollback to previous model variant and restart traffic steering to baseline fleet (owner: SRE)
  4) Collect logs and trace samples; open JIRA (prefix RE-rollback)

Post-dry-run evidence capture:
- Save sample request traces for 30 minutes before and after each ramp
- Export cost telemetry for the run window
- Snapshot autoscaler events and k8s events (control plane)
- Collect model inference artifact manifests and kernel selection logs

Draft release notes (for later polishing) - do not publish without approvals:
- Summary: "Runtime and model rollout: serving-runtime v3.4.1 + model xg-7b-v2"
- Highlights:
  - Improved KV cache warmup reduces first-token latency by ~14% in long-tail workloads
  - Autoscaler policy tuned to reduce scale-up oscillation for bursty inference patterns
  - New model variant xg-7b-v2: better handling of structured tool outputs and lower hallucination on code prompts
- Migration steps for customers:
  - No breaking API changes. Customers using internal caching heuristics may see faster cold-starts; we recommend testing QPS patterns against staging.
- Known issues (temporary):
  - Under specific synthetic workloads, P95 shows a transient bump during first 10 minutes after ramp (workaround: stagger the initial ramp by 5 minutes)
  - Embedding canonicalization edge-case where very short inputs produce high-similarity collisions - tracked in JIRA RE-4389

Red-team/observability notes:
- Query set to validate: latency_by_route, error_by_model_variant, autoscale_events, cost_per_token_hourly
- Save synthetic prompts used for automated evals alongside the run artifacts

Runbook aftermath TODOs (example owner assignments):
- Marcus Lee: bake the final canary config into infra repo and add comment with rollback window (due: +3d)
- Sofia Ramirez: add synthetic evals to nightly-suite and create dashboard panels (due: +5d)
- Owen Zhang: follow up on autoscaler logs and add additional metrics for GPU throttling (due: +2d)
- Priya Kapoor: draft customer-facing note with migration guidance (due: +7d)

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep the dry-run small if we have on-call churn; nothing worse than doing a dry-run during an unrelated P0.
- If the automation path fails at check1, we should abort and re-run after postmortem — try not to trust manual hotfixes unless runway >2h.

Appendix: quick links and checkpoints
- Confluence preflight index (linked above)
- Infra PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/1124
- Incident template: confluence:RE/Incident-template
- Example JIRA keys opened during rehearsal: RE-5020, RE-5021 (placeholder)

End of prototype doc. Please add observations from the dry-run below and move status to in_review once the retro is complete.
